Complete the following activity to form a quadratic equation whose roots are \(5\) and \(12\).
solution:
The roots are \(5\) and \(12\).
Sum of roots \(= 5 + 12 = 17\).
Product of roots \(= 5 \times 12 = 60\).
The standard form is \(x^2 - (\text{sum of roots})x + (\text{product of roots}) = 0\).
\(\therefore x^2 - 17x + 60 = 0\) is the required quadratic equation.

subtopic: Shares — Face Value, Market Value, Brokerage
stem: Pushpmala has invested ₹24,000 and purchased shares of FV ₹20 at a premium of ₹4. Complete the following activity to find the number of shares she purchased.
solution:
\(FV = ₹20\), Premium \(= ₹4\).
\(MV = FV + \text{Premium} = 20 + 4 = ₹24\).
Number of shares \(= \dfrac{\text{Total investment}}{MV} = \dfrac{24000}{24} = 1000\) shares.

stem: Solve the following simultaneous equations: \(x + y = 3\); \(3x - 2y = 4\).
solution: From \(x + y = 3\), we get \(x = 3 - y\). Substitute in \(3x - 2y = 4\): \(3(3 - y) - 2y = 4 \Rightarrow 9 - 3y - 2y = 4 \Rightarrow 9 - 5y = 4 \Rightarrow 5y = 5 \Rightarrow y = 1\). Then \(x = 3 - 1 = 2\). \(\therefore x = 2, y = 1\).

subtopic: Shares — Face Value, Market Value, Brokerage
stem: A share is sold for the market value of ₹2,000. Brokerage is paid at the rate of 0.5%. What is the amount received after the sale?
solution: Brokerage \(= 0.5\% \text{ of } 2000 = \dfrac{0.5}{100} \times 2000 = ₹10\). On selling, the brokerage is deducted, so amount received \(= 2000 - 10 = ₹1990\).
